name: team_planning_attention
description: List what needs attention in a scenario of a Team Planning plan the caller is in: changes that still resolve but no longer fit, often because a scenario it follows changed later. Each item has the subject_id and facet that no longer fit (a person's assignment, a position, a unit, a succession, a reporting line, a budget line, a position's funding, a cost centre with its name as subject_id (no_cost_centre for seats with none), the whole budget with the plan's id as subject_id, or a place's capacity as capacity:<unit or position id>, or capacity:unassigned for someone in no unit), a reason, and the change it belongs to: its kind, the scenario that made it and its event_id. That is the later to land of the subject's own change and the change that broke it, such as a parent unit's retirement; change is null when nothing in the plan explains it. It also checks each person: placed nowhere, over or under 100% allocated (an unknown total is neither), still in the plan after the Org Graph has them leave, no manager (except the head of the tree), or a manager who is gone, has left, or is in or owns none of their units nor the unit directly above one. In a plan scoped to chosen units, each change about someone the plan no longer covers is listed under that change's facet, unnamed, because a bring-in was undone or the Org Graph moved them out; clear the change or place them back in. Once a capacity model is chosen for any role or family, even one no place takes, each place no model covers is listed too, except a leaver's, a forgotten person's override and a closed position's. A seat whose reports cost more to manage than it delivers, a person or an open position, is listed once under the facet capacity, overridden or not. In a scenario with budget lines it also checks the budget: a held position no line matches, or two lines tie for, with no funding set; a seat held in the period with no cost centre, once a line or seat in the plan has one; a person costed in one cost centre while the cost centre entries that match them, their position, or a budget line it draws on names another; a line, cost centre or the whole budget over its approved amount or head count, judged at the budget strictness rule's scope; and a line in the period nothing draws on or ties for. No budget item names an amount, and a line, cost centre or budget over its approved amount is flagged only to a member with the see-pay right. `sources` names where to fix each item: the provider of employment status for someone who joined after the base or has left, the provider of the manager fact for a manager item, else the providers of the units the item touches ("espalia" for a unit only the plan holds). Items come grouped by check, named in each item's `check`, in this order: placements, positions, units, unresolved, uncovered, successions, capacity_overrides, allocations, leavers, managers, overloaded, unclassified, budget_lines, fundings, unfunded, ambiguous_funding, unplaced, cost_centre_mismatches, budget_variance, unused_budget_lines; then by subject_id and reason. Fix an item with a new change, or by pinning or clearing one. `names` maps each subject the scenario's map holds to the name the map shows: a person's (a placeholder hire's label), a unit's, a position's such as "Backfill: Software Engineer", or a succession's as its units before and after. A forgotten person reads as "Former member", a removed placeholder label as "Placeholder hire", and a unit, position or succession the map no longer holds has no name. An archived plan is not checked: it returns checked: false, archived_on and a note, with nothing listed, so an empty list never reads as nothing wrong. Restoring the plan checks it again; otherwise checked is true. Refused, as an unknown plan, unless the caller is a member.

scenario_id.description: The scenario, or the plan's id for the baseline. Omit it for the baseline.
